### PowerDetect UV Reveal

I was surprised how much I liked the AI-powered Shark PowerDetect UV Reveal. Its UV light revealed spots on my floor where I know I previously had spills, and its built-in AI had the vacuum go back over to deep-clean those spots in a way I clearly hadn’t done before. The UV Reveal also did a great job on my hard floors (both LVP and tile) as a mop-and-vacuum combo, as well as on my builder-grade carpet and a large rug in the living room. I was impressed that the rug actually felt just as fluffy and well-vacuumed as if I had cracked out my favorite Dyson stick vacuum instead of just sending a robot vacuum to do the work for me.

...

Eufy

### Omni C28

If you’re looking for vacuuming and mopping but don’t want to pay close to or beyond a four-figure sum, this is the vacuum to choose. Former WIRED editor Adrienne So previously recommended Eufy’s older X10 Pro Omni as a great robot vacuum without spending too much, and Eufy released the Eufy Omni C28 at the end of February with a similar set of features and price point. The Omni C28 comes with nearly double the suction power of the older model, a self-cleaning roller mop instead of mop pads, and retractable detangling brushes.

It does a solid job mopping and vacuuming, but it has a shorter battery life, leaving it at only 37 percent after completing the four-room main floor of my house. This is a bit of a bummer, since this affordable vacuum can do multi-floor mapping. While it can store enough maps to clean all three levels of my home, it doesn’t have the battery life to do so. But it does charge fairly quickly, and I was able to still clean all three floors of my house in a single day—I just had to let it recharge a little at the base first. It went back up to 57 percent battery life after just 20 minutes in its docking station. It also tried to eat the cords near my bed, and luckily I was nearby to yank them free. If you get this vacuum, make sure your cords are clear of the vacuum's reach.

With my corner Cheerio test, this vacuum also got two out of three Cheerios, but it missed the trickier fridge-corner Cheerio. This is the hardest spot to get into, so I’m not surprised, but it does mean you’ll have to check those corners more with this vacuum. The cherry juice spill test also showed similar results: the first spot it reached was cleaned completely, while the second spot, which had more time to dry, still had some sticky residue left behind.

Overall, though, it’s a good vacuum for the price, especially since it packs multi-floor mapping, the capability to mop and vacuum, and good results all around for a vacuum that’s already usually on sale for around $500.

...

### Qrevo 2 Pro

Roborock

If the Eufy isn't on sale (which is rare), I'd get this vacuum instead. The Roborock Qrevo 2 Pro is the newest update to Roborock's more affordable Qrevo line that went without updates for years. The Qrevo 2 Pro is cheaper than the Curv 2 that launched back in January 2026 and still packs a ton of power, great navigation, and the same handy app. It comes with 20,000 Pa of suction, a FlexiArm mop that does a better job corner cleaning, and a reversible side brush to help dislodge corner debris.

It's technically the same price as the Eufy Omni C28, but the Eufy is usually on sale for a hefty discount. It's still early days for the Qrevo 2 Pro since it launched at the end of August, so if it starts going on sale more often, I'll label it as a true budget buy. (It has gone on sale once already and was a little cheaper than the Eufy.) There are a few contrasts to consider between the two similarly priced vacuums that came up in my testing. The Eufy got itself stuck on cords in my bedroom, while the Qrevo 2 Pro only attempted to eat cords without actually getting stuck on them. The Qrevo still isn't great at seeing small objects; it took my cat's toys for rides around the room, but they usually didn't get stuck or stop the vacuum.

Both scored a 2 out of 3 on my Cheerio test, but the Qrevo 2 Pro got the harder fridge Cheerio with its FlexiArm mop. However, the Eufy did better on mopping, cleaning most of the spills entirely. I'm giving the Qrevo 2 Pro a 1.25 out of 2—one spill was just about gone, but the area around it was all slightly sticky, while the second spill was only half cleaned. It's hard to perfectly grade. It also tends to leave some debris behind when it goes over thresholds that separate carpet from hard flooring, but it didn't have this issue when transitioning onto rugs.

But my favorite is how quiet this vacuum is. Both the base station and vacuum itself are quieter than the Eufy Omni C28, and it is especially pleasant if you let the Qrevo 2 Pro vacuum and mop separately. It takes longer than doing the combo cleans, but this vacuum pulled off doing both a separate vacuuming session and mopping of my massive first floor in two hours, which most vacuums still take for combo cleans. Overall it's a good vacuum, and it's especially worth snagging when on sale.
